mark.claim: Schönhage and Strassen gave a multiplication method with running time $O(n\log n\log\log n)$
mark.quote: proved in 1971 that two $n$-bit integers can be multiplied in $O(n\log n\log\log n)$ time

mark.claim: It is the
mark.quote: unconditional $O(n\log n)$ upper bound
mark.paragraph: The Harvey–van der Hoeven multiplier is a deterministic algorithm that multiplies two $n$-bit integers in worst-case time $O(n\log n)$ on a multitape Turing machine, a machine with several tapes, each read and written by its own head. It is the for integer multiplication, so it needs no unproven hypothesis.

mark.claim: Its value is $2^{-182}$
mark.paragraph: The target's bound is $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ for a fixed constant $\kappa>0$. Its value is $2^{-182}$. Since $(\lg n)^{1-\kappa}/\lg n=(\lg n)^{-\kappa}$ tends to $0$ as $n\to\infty$, the target's bound grows strictly slower than $n\log n$.

mark.claim: Hence multiplication by a power of $y$ is a signed cyclic shift of the list
mark.quote: multiplication by such a root is a signed shift of the coefficient list
mark.paragraph: Multiplying by $y$ moves each entry up one place, and the entry at degree $r-1$ wraps to degree $0$ with a minus sign, as in the example. Since $y^k=-y^{k-r}$ for $r\le k<2r$ and $y^{2r}=1$, every power of $y$ acts this way some number of times. Hence multiplication by a power of $y$ is a signed cyclic shift of the list.

mark.claim: The ring therefore computes a cyclic convolution
mark.quote: its negative wrap gives precisely the original cyclic wrap after the twist is removed
mark.paragraph: The cyclic form matters because of the polynomial ring. Let $\sigma$ be a coefficient position, from $0$ to $n-1$. In $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ with $r=n$, a product term past the top coefficient picks up a minus sign, since $y^r=-1$. A phase twist removes this sign: multiply the coefficient of $y^\sigma$ by $\zeta^\sigma$ before the product, and by $\zeta^{-\sigma}$ after it. Let $\alpha$ be the coefficient at $y^{\sigma+n}$ in the twisted product. That term wraps to $-\alpha\zeta^{-\sigma}y^\sigma$ after the untwist, and $-\alpha\zeta^{-\sigma}=\alpha\zeta^{-(\sigma+n)}$ because $\zeta^n=-1$, which is the untwisted term moved to $y^\sigma$. The ring therefore computes a cyclic convolution.

mark.claim: The paper's assembly section gives the exact binary product this way
mark.quote: propagates carries to obtain the exact binary product
mark.paragraph: Exact recovery by rounding inverts the [Signed Kronecker packing](kronecker-packing.md), which evaluates the coefficients at $2^b$. Let $\delta_j$ be the $j$-th radix-$2^b$ digit of the integer being formed and $\sigma_j$ the carry into position $j$. Set $\sigma_0=0$ and, for each $j$, choose $\delta_j$ and $\sigma_{j+1}$ so that $\rho_j+\sigma_j=\delta_j+2^b\sigma_{j+1}$ with $0\le\delta_j<2^b$. Multiplying the $j$-th relation by $2^{bj}$ and summing, the carries cancel in pairs, so the digits represent the same integer as $\sum_j\rho_j2^{bj}$, with the final carry written as further digits. The paper's assembly section gives the exact binary product this way.

judged.label: partial
judged.reason: The quotation says carries are propagated to obtain the exact binary product, but not the specific radix-2^b digit and carry construction (delta_j, sigma_{j+1}, cancellation) that 'this way' refers to.
